sections.h2: 10 kW solar system price in Pakistan
p: A 10 kW on-grid system, the most common size for a house with two or three ACs, was quoted at Rs 950,000 to Rs 1,200,000 installed. Panels are about Rs 400,000 to Rs 455,000 of that; the inverter is usually the next biggest line, then the structure and installation. A hybrid 10 kW system with a lithium battery costs more; see the hybrid example below.

Prices in this range normally include tier-one panels, an on-grid inverter, a galvanised structure, DC and AC cabling with breakers and surge protection, earthing, installation and the net billing application. Elevated structures, long cable runs and sales tax are often extra.

sections.h2: 3 kW and 5 kW solar system price
p: Large systems cost less per watt than small ones because the inverter, structure, labour and paperwork are spread over more panels: a 3 kW system is about Rs 100 to Rs 167 per watt and a 20 kW system about Rs 90 to Rs 110. Between neighbouring small sizes the price lists do not always follow this rule, so compare quotes for your exact size. If your roof and sanctioned load allow it, a slightly larger system is often better value per watt.

Use the solar system size calculator to find the size your bill needs before pricing it; an oversized on-grid system exports units at the buyback rate, which is far below the price you pay for imported units.

sections.h2: Solar system on installments: what the payback means
p: Banks and installers offer solar on monthly installments. The simple payback above tells you whether the installment can be lower than the bill it replaces: a 10 kW system paying back in 3.2 to 4 years at Rs 25,000 a month of savings leaves little room for financing cost over a short term, more over a longer one. Compare the total installment cost, not the monthly figure, with the cash price.

Payback here is simple: price divided by yearly saving. It does not include panel degradation, tariff changes, maintenance or interest. Use it to rank options, then ask for a written quote and check it with the quote checker; the solar price tracker shows how these prices have moved month by month.

faq.q: What is the price of a 10 kW solar system in Pakistan?
faq.a: About Rs 950,000 to Rs 1,200,000 installed for an on-grid system in the installer price lists and reports we checked (date under Sources), that is Rs 95 to Rs 120 per watt. A hybrid system with a battery costs more.

faq.q: How much does a 5 kW solar system cost?
faq.a: About Rs 550,000 to Rs 900,000 installed on-grid. Per watt it is dearer than a 10 kW system because the fixed parts of the job are spread over fewer panels.

faq.q: How much does a 3 kW solar system cost?
faq.a: About Rs 300,000 to Rs 500,000 installed on-grid, around Rs 100 to Rs 167 per watt. Hybrid versions with a small battery cost noticeably more.

faq.q: Is a hybrid solar system worth the extra price?
faq.a: If you have loadshedding and need backup, yes: the battery replaces a UPS. If your supply is reliable and net billing is available, an on-grid system gives the shortest payback. Compare the battery kWh and warranty separately from the per-watt price.

faq.q: Can I get a solar system on installments?
faq.a: Yes, through banks and some installers. Work out the simple payback first, then compare the total of all installments with the cash price; a short-term loan can cost more per month than the bill it replaces.

faq.q: Why do prices differ so much between installers?
faq.a: Panel and inverter brands, structure type, cable sizes, protection, warranty years and what is left out of the quote. Our ranges come from secondary sources and change monthly; always get three written quotes and check them with the quote checker.

key_facts: A 10 kW on-grid solar system was quoted at about Rs 950,000 to Rs 1,200,000 installed in Pakistan in the price lists and reports Wattlyst checked on the date under Sources, that is Rs 95 to Rs 120 per watt.
Tier-one panels alone cost about Rs 40.00 to Rs 45.50 per watt; the inverter, structure, cables, protection, labour and net billing paperwork make up the rest of an installed price.

Price per watt is lower for large systems than for small ones, although sources disagree between neighbouring sizes: a 3 kW system is about Rs 100 to Rs 167 per watt, a 20 kW system about Rs 90 to Rs 110.
Simple payback = installed price ÷ yearly bill saving; it ignores panel degradation, tariff changes and financing cost, so treat it as a first screen, not a forecast.
These are secondary-source market prices (installer lists, news, price guides), not an official rate; they move with the rupee, panel prices and tax policy and are refreshed monthly.
mistakes: Comparing a hybrid quote with an on-grid price. The battery and hybrid inverter can add a third or more.
Pricing before sizing. Size the system from your bill first; an oversized on-grid system exports at the buyback rate.
Forgetting the extras. Elevated structure, long AC runs, civil work and sales tax are often outside the quoted price.
Reading the payback as a promise. It ignores degradation, tariff changes and financing; use it to compare options.
